samples.summary: Preview idempotency is keyed on family alone, so a second row that paints MORE glyphs in the same family is silently skipped — the acceptance criterion "the subset covers every character the row actually paints" can fail across surfaces
samples.evidence: `if (findPreviewFontLink(family)) return;` dedupes purely by family name, ignoring `text`. The picker dropdown row paints only the label (`{entry.label}`, font-family-picker.tsx:260) while the MoreFontsDialog row paints label + group name (the button carries `style={{fontFamily}}`, more-fonts-dialog.tsx:245-250). Open the picker first (subset = "Open Sans") and then the "More fonts…" dialog: the dialog's observer no-ops against the existing narrower subset, so "Sans-serif" renders from the fallback face — exactly the two-faces-on-one-line bug acceptance criterion 3 exists to prevent. The union of glyphs (or a text-aware key / widening re-request) is not implemented.

samples.summary: Recent rows for families outside the curated catalog carry no weight, so the preview falls back to wght@400 — the exact failure mode acceptance criteria 2 and 5 call out
samples.evidence: `data-font-weights={entry?.weights}` uses `CATALOG_BY_FAMILY` (the ~105-entry curated catalog). A family picked from the 1,908-entry full library is stored by `addRecentFont` as a bare string (font-recents.ts:53 stores names only) and is absent from the curated index, so `entry` is undefined, the attribute is absent, and `ensurePreviewFontLink` falls through to `previewWeight(undefined)` → `DEFAULT_WEIGHTS.split(';')[0]` → `400`. For a full-library family that ships no 400 cut (`Buda` 300, `UnifrakturCook` 700 — both named in the issue), css2 answers HTTP 400 and the row is stranded in a fallback face. Criterion 5 explicitly requires the weight be derived from what the row renders rather than a curated-catalog lookup that may miss.

samples.summary: Canonical design docs still describe the preview path as `ensureFontLink`; the loading-model change is recorded only in the source docstring and in docs/tasks, not folded into the subsystem design docs
samples.evidence: slides-fonts.md:177-184 and :201-202 ("Each visible row previews in its own family via an IntersectionObserver that calls `ensureFontLink` only for on-screen rows") and docs/design/docs/docs-font-controls.md:164 ("lazy-loads its CSS via `ensureFontLink(family, weights)` the first time a family is picked, hovered, or previewed") are now factually wrong: previewing goes through the new `ensurePreviewFontLink` with a new DOM contract (`data-wafflebase-font-preview`) and glyph subsetting. Neither doc, nor the `font-catalog.ts` row of the file table (docs-font-controls.md:76), was updated. Nested design docs are not link/ref-checked by CI, so nothing else catches this.

samples.summary: Comment contradicts the mechanism it introduces
samples.evidence: "Subset to the row's own text: a preview only ever paints the label" — the code deliberately reads the whole row's `textContent` precisely because a row can paint more than its label (the dialog's sibling comment says the opposite). Misleading for the next reader who considers narrowing the subset back to the label.

samples.summary: Unrelated ref→state fix for the dialog's IntersectionObserver root is bundled into a byte-reduction change
samples.evidence: Switching `scrollRef` to `setScrollEl` state (and adding `scrollEl` to the effect deps) fixes whether the dialog's preview observer ever arms at all — a pre-existing behaviour bug orthogonal to glyph subsetting. It is defensible (the new test needs a live observer) but it is scope beyond the issue's outcome and would be clearer as its own change or at least called out in the PR description.

samples.summary: Preview requests a single weight while rows may render at a different weight, a small deviation from the issue's "font rendering is unchanged" promise
samples.evidence: `previewWeight` takes only the first cut, whereas the full load requested the whole `weights` spec (e.g. `400;700`). Selected rows render with `font-medium` (more-fonts-dialog.tsx:243) and checked picker items may be bolded; with only one cut available the browser synthesises or snaps rather than using the shipped face. Impact is likely imperceptible, but it is a rendering difference the issue said would not occur.

verdict.reason:
The quoted code exists exactly as described (font-catalog.ts:227 `if (findPreviewFontLink(family)) return;`, keyed on family only), and the two call sites differ in painted text as claimed (font-family-picker.tsx:260 paints only the label inside the `[data-font-row]` item; more-fonts-dialog.tsx:245-250 sets `fontFamily` on the button so the group-name span at 248-250 inherits it). So the described cross-surface narrowing interaction is mechanically real. It is nevertheless not a blocking finding under the design-fit / spec-conformance rubric, for two grounded reasons.

(1) The repo's originating spec artifact prescribes the flagged guard verbatim. docs/tasks/active/20260825-font-preview-subset-todo.md:33-34 requires: "It keeps `ensureFontLink`'s other guards: SSR, system fonts, eager bootstrap families, and **idempotency per family**." A family-keyed dedupe is therefore the specified approach, not scope creep or a wrong abstraction. The acceptance item that actually addresses glyph coverage is todo:39-43 ("The subset text is read from the row's own `textContent`, not from a catalog lookup … This also covers `MoreFontsDialog`'s group-name span"), and both observers implement it (font-family-picker.tsx:123-127 and more-fonts-dialog.tsx:151-155 pass `row.textContent ?? ""`). The verifiable acceptance criteria in this repository are met; the "union of glyphs / text-aware key" the finding demands is nowhere requested, and todo:58-62 further narrows scope ("Out of scope: any change to `ensureFontLink` / `findFontLink`"). The intended per-family (text-independent) dedupe is also pinned by an existing test: ensure-font-link.test.ts:136-139 calls `ensurePreviewFontLink(FAKE_A, 'One')` twice plus FAKE_B and asserts exactly 2 links.

(2) What remains after (1) is a cache-key edge case in one function producing a narrower-than-needed `&text=` payload in a specific open-picker-then-open-dialog sequence. That is a line-level logic/correctness defect, which the design-fit lens explicitly defers ("NOT your lane … Line-level logic bugs (correctness lens)"). It is not a spec mismatch, not duplication of an existing module, not a wrong layer, and not a missing/parallel design doc. Refuted as out-of-scope for this lens only — the correctness lens is the right home for it.

verdict.reason: Verified as described. font-family-picker.tsx:46-48 indexes only the 105-entry curated FONT_CATALOG, and the Recent rows (215-233) set data-font-weights={entry?.weights} from that map. font-recents.ts:53-66 persists recents as bare family strings (written by applyPick, which also serves full-library dialog picks at :281), so a family from the 1,908-entry font-catalog.full.ts has no entry and the attribute is absent. The observer passes row.dataset.fontWeights (:126) to ensurePreviewFontLink, whose own lookup is the same curated CATALOG_INDEX (font-catalog.ts:91-93, 223), so previewWeight(undefined) returns DEFAULT_WEIGHTS.split(';')[0] = 400 (font-catalog.ts:95, 184-187). Buda (weights "300", font-catalog.full.ts:261) and UnifrakturCook (weights "700", :1816) are absent from font-catalog.data.ts, so their preview requests ask for a weight the family does not ship. No guard prevents it: the findFontLink no-op (font-catalog.ts:226) only applies when a full link already exists in the current page, while recents survive reloads and fullCatalog is fetched only when the More-fonts dialog opens (font-family-picker.tsx:87-100). This fails the explicit acceptance criteria in docs/tasks/active/20260825-font-preview-subset-todo.md:35-38 ("Weight is derived from the entry's weights, never hardcoded to 400") and :44-45 (both observers pass a data-font-weights attribute), with :39-43 stating recents/full library contain families absent from CATALOG_INDEX — a spec-conformance gap, so it is in-lane and major.

The canonical design docs still attribute previewing to `ensureFontLink`/`data-wafflebase-font`: slides-fonts.md:177-184 ("selection, picker hover, or in-view preview in the dialog… data-wafflebase-font attribute") and :201-202 ("IntersectionObserver that calls `ensureFontLink` only for on-screen rows"), and docs-font-controls.md:163-165 ("lazy-loads its CSS via `ensureFontLink(family, weights)` the first time a family is picked, hovered, or previewed") plus the file table row at :76.
